# End of the year retro

## Things that affect the team negatively 
- Layoffs 
- Due to extra work incurred 
- Announcements about having a great year but also laying off 10% of the workforce
- Adopting chatops was stressful; this team didn’t have the capacity, and it took months of work to stabilize 

## Management response to incidents 
The panic around availability and incidents and the hyper-focus affect team morale more than the actual incidents. 
The team also feels it cares about availability and doesn’t need the extra prioritization. 

## Things that we were surprised didn’t affect the team as much.
- Re-orgs - nobody cares
- Q3 workload - compared to layoffs, this didn’t seem that bad.
- Incidents themselves - incidents are a great learning opportunity. Focusing on incidents has helped the team understand the system and grow knowledge. The group is generally pleased with our product availability and resilience. 

## Moving forwards
- There was a downward trend in team health during layoffs and the availability scare, but generally, the trend is positive.
- We need product support, and the team needs to learn how to work with the product. We are building a platform with little product input, and that’s concerning. 
- The team is excited to have more new team members and is thankful for other teams’ contributions to helping with work.
- The team is excited to add new integrators. Some of the hard work on the new platform is beginning to pay off.
